You need:

  • A case
  • A power supply (sometimes included with the case)
  • A mainboard
  • A processor
  • A frocessor fan (often included with the processor)
  • RAM
  • A graphics card (there are mothermoards with integrated graphics, but those aren't good enough for gaming IMO)
  • Storage, a harddisk or SSD

The mainboard limits which processors and RAM you can use. Make sure the case is big enough for the motherboard and the graphics card.

I'll need to see your budget, then maybe I can help more effectively :)

I suggest you go with either a Fury X if you want to game smoothly on 4k or the 980ti if you want to game smoothly on lower resolutions (1080/1440). For the CPU, a 4790k would do great.

The GPU+CPU combo would cost $1000 on average, so lets move on to other components.

A high-end ~$150 z97 motherboard. I'd personally recommend Asus, but others like Gigabyte/MSI/ASRock/EVGA are all good as well. A 750W PSU would be sufficient, just go for those priced from $70 and above since I'm afraid that cheaper ones have lousy transistors. Trusted brands are FSP/SeaSonic/Corsair/EVGA, other mentionable ones are CoolerMaster and SilverStone. For RAM, 2x4GB sticks should be enough. For storage, you might want to opt for an SSD and a HDD. Since SSDs are fast, use that to install your OS and frequently used programs so that your overall experience would be faster. Since the HDD is slower, you might want to install other minor data in it like Music or Documents. Any case with decent airflow and cable management is good enough. I suggest you look at Corsair/CoolerMaster/Fractal Design for good quality cases.

Don't worry :)

Most of the assembly part is quite self explanatory so you'll less likely be able to screw up, but as always, when in doubt, lookout for YouTube vids.

Some precautions to take note:

  • Don't let Thermal paste get onto the motherboard, this usually happens when people put too much. Just the size of a rice grain on the CPU should do the trick.
  • Don't force too hard on the CPU into the socket. Be VERY gentle with it, or else you'll get bent pins. If you do get bent pins like what happened to me, you'll be happy to know that a normal credit card has the exact thickness to match the gaps between the pins, so straightening them out with a credit card is a breeze.
